verdict.tagline: Massive multiplayer battles bogged down by technical friction.
for_you_if: you want large scale team combat
you can overlook missing historical factions
not_for_you_if: you will not install a third party launcher
you need stable frame rates on release hardware

claims.claim: Reviewers experience technical performance issues including frame rate drops, stuttering, and screen snapping to the sky.

citations.review_text: good game has a nice Great graphics, but it's a RAM hog. It consumes a lot ram i got 16gb and sh!t a lot of drop frames + if u play on windows 11 gg
good game but customization sucks ass and it's an absolute stutter fest no matter what i try
The stuttering is just insane

Its 2026 and this game is a pretty decent title.
You can tell where EA skimped on the details of this one.  Less destruction on the map, graphics not as good as Battlefield 1, Sound is your typical battlefield game.  The gun mechanics feel a little off on this one, but nothing that is going to stop you from playing this first-person shooter.  

The one thing that plagued this game for me and made it a total pain in the butt, was the constant screen snapping to the sky.  After trying this and that with the controller, unplugging the mouse, trying a new USB slot for the controller, turning Steam controller input off and on again, nothing seemed to stop this bug from happening randomly every couple min.  What did finally work for me and stop the screen snapping to the sky was going into the EA App itself, going into settings and turning the in-game overlay off.  After I did that, the game stopped looking to the sky.  I wish I would have tried this when I was playing Battlefield 1. 

Because of the story missions, this game does have a moderate amount of replay value.


Would I recommend this game: Yes
What do I rate this game: 4/5

claims.claim: Reviewers mention that the single-player campaign relies heavily on stealth mechanics.

citations.review_text:
Underrated game. Gunplay feels so smooth. 
Singleplayer is mainly stealth (which I’m not fan of). But multiplayer is great. There are, still, full servers. Sometimes you need to wait in queue to join one 😅. 

Nevertheless 9/10

attlefield V may never have reached the same legendary status as Battlefield 1, but it's still a very good Battlefield game. The gunplay is among the best in the series, movement feels faster and more fluid than ever, squad play is rewarding, and the destruction, visuals, and sound design remain absolutely top-tier. After years of updates, the multiplayer has become a genuinely solid experience with a great selection of maps and weapons.

The campaign, however, is a mixed bag. Like Battlefield 1, it uses War Stories, but the episodes are less memorable overall and rely too heavily on stealth. That said, The Last Tiger is exceptional and easily one of the strongest single-player stories DICE has ever produced, while Tirailleur is also worth experiencing. The rest ranges from decent to forgettable and never reaches the emotional impact of Battlefield 1.

It may not surpass its predecessor in atmosphere or storytelling, but beneath the rocky launch lies an excellent WWII shooter with outstanding gameplay. A flawed sequel, yet one that's well worth revisiting.

citations.review_text: My experience with battlefield 5 has totally turned me off in the whole battlefield experience the single player is frustrating to play not enjoyable at all many of the binded keys do not function

This game should be known by its online mode. I played a few times with friend and it was a lot of fun. Each map is based on a real battle in the history of WWII, and you have many options to fight, using guns, driving tanks/cars/planes, and it is even better when playing with friends.

But I'm a single player lover, so I mostly play war story.

The story is very great and special. They are not some well-known big battles, instead it picks some less known and very special histories, like bank robber being recruited by UK, African soldiers fighting in France, the last Tiger tank. And I love it very much how this game tell these stories in a very immersive way. All stories left significant impression on me, and they make people reflect about wars and humanity.

However, the story game play is so buggy. There are a lot of times when I collected all collectables but the challenge was not accomplished, or I have destroyed some of the targets (like searchlights in the Norway story), but after I died I need to redo them again. It feels like some important milestones (especially those tracked by challenges) are not carefully processed and stored.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that official servers across Asia have been blocked, leaving the multiplayer mode reliant on community servers with very low player counts.

citations.review_text:
This is an extremely solid Battlefield entry, even when they returned back to WW2 roots. I didn't get to know the franchise closer and played it in their rocky releases and life cycles, so this is coming from a new player, picking this up for the first time, after the life cycle ended. I admit, I'm a huge sucker for WW2 as a general setting, so obviously, when the depiction of the most horrific war in human history constantly goes into $2 sales, I had to pick it up.

Gameplay is surprisingly good, especially for a game this age. It still delivers stunning graphics without being overly demanding on hardware, a baseline modern casual FPS game mechanics and loop, without an egregiously low or high TTK, and obviously, the experience of infantry and vehicle battles. You cannot go wrong picking this game up when it's on sale, because that is also when new player population and the overall player count will peak. As for game modes, it's bog standard for Battlefield, Conquest and Breakthrough being the main stars, and they two overshadows every other game mode significantly. Anything else that isn't Conquest or Breakthrough will be very hard to find unless you found an already populated server. Game modes aside, the connection and responsiveness is very good, especially for a large multiplayer shooter.

Games get older, but their players got sharper, so you're definitely in for a hell of a ride without ropes. I am speaking on behalf of Asian servers player (because that's where I'm coming from), that you will find some of the most heinous, KD glazing, top frag seeking sweats on any servers, guaranteed. Whether they're on foot or in a vehicle, they couldn't care less for teamwork in a game so intrinsically tied to that concept and wants their position on the leaderboard to be earned with kills. It will be an uphill battle against them, especially when they're dominating with a vehicle. Not fun, yes, but unfortunately it's part of aging games. So you would need to prepare you…

This game has blocked all official servers across Asia, so now it can only be played on community servers. However, there are very few people playing on the community servers, so the multiplayer mode is basically empty. This game is done for.

In fact, they noted a glitch exploit that allows people to fire the anti-tank rifles super fast, game breakingly fast, and they officially said "No that's fine" because it's no longer their bread winner, and they don't want to put in the effort to fix literally anything.

  If you like cheating while AFK, then this is the game for you!  You'll never get in trouble for cheating or using racism or anything!  If you're an honest player, this game is insufferable unless you're highly intoxicated.  I wish your liver the best of luck.

This is still one of the best BFs ever, the game goes on sale often and still has a decent amount of players.

There are hackers but you can avoid them by using the server filter and looking for ROBOT servers which help exclude hackers a LOT.

I think it's a solid game. 
Singleplayer has some fun levels with a nod to historical event's (but of course very gamified) but playing it through Hardcore was very very bad, just constantly staying in cover and peaking for a second before I have to get back and recover hp.

Multiplayer is fine too, I like the upgrade/attachment system more than the one from BF1, but of course it's not as interesting as BF4 or 3, although with WW2 weapons they don't really have much room to paly with. I do like the gunplay, but also wish bipod mg's were a little bit better. the game feels more run and gun compared to previous ones and it makes it harder for them to shine. And the overall balance for those doesn't feel bad either.

Vehicles are more diverse between nations, each having unique ones with different upgrades but they don't feel toooo different. Plus I like the change to them having a limited amount of ammo and hp they can repair before they have to return to a repair station. Planes can be really ass to be against tho.

The maps are overall ok, but I don't think I have a favorite, nor one I would love to see in a different BF title.


Despite all of this, I find BFV to be not as entertaining as previous titles. It also has some hackers/cheaters and for some reason no Italian or Soviet forces, which is a massive disappointment imo.

So far there are enough players to find a bunch of active servers, but once they are gone I wouldn't recommend this game.

Only thing is the dying player base but apart from that is is awesome and would highly recommend especially if your into WW2.

Never agreed with the initial backlash this game got, i've played my fair share of BF games but always disliked the fandom for causing this game's early death for such a stupid reasons (Though firestorm is undeniably a mess and waste of resources, and should have never happened lol i blame EA)
Breakthrough is one of the best shooter gamemodes i've played, it's a fun, varied, and chaotic challenge and has less chances of having steamroll matches by having "controlled" chaos
Conquest might be the poster gamemode but i think BF shines in this controlled chaos of Breakthrough, flank and choke points are (most of the time) fair and make for a great push and pull challenge between defense and attackers and i would have loved for this game to get more Maps designed specifically for Breakthrough, or well, more maps at all.
Movement feels incredible, it's smooth and diegetic, the systems of reviving, health and ammo recovery, squad reviving, vehicle resupply are the best additions for BF games, make for an amazing immersive experience in beautiful maps, that while some might complain its saturated, i think it makes for an amazing contrast and experience
Visuals are to this day (2026) incredible, other than the pop-in and Rtx glitches (hey, it was a pioneer!) there's not much to complain (the smoke is amazing! and they know it since its a main part of breaking a chokepoint!)
Shooters are usually my "junk food", but i can really recommend this one
i wish this had the same amount of maps as BF1, and the actual Operations mode from it (Grand Ops is just not the same)
BFV and BF1 are peak BF and peak DICE

Battlefield 1942 may still be the GOAT, but Battlefield V is a very good installment in the Battlefield series. The guns shoot well and the music remains truly fantastic: both the theme track and in-game music.

Additionally, the game is very well optimized for PCs. Unlike other games from so-called AAA developers, I rarely experience frame drops and stutters while playing in 4K with high graphics.

As of 2026, dozens of servers with plenty of players can still be found. I mainly play the Breakthrough game mode, which is highly recommended. I highly recommend buying this game!
